precepts.text: Israel is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure. This goes with the certain vessel descending in the dream.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
In the dream Peter “saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners”. What is that vessel? Hosea says it: “Israel is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.”

Israel is the vessel. Swallowed up among the nations, a vessel no one has pleasure in: that is what came down to Peter in the sheet.

That is why the dream was never about eating unclean animals. Verse 28 is where Peter breaks the dream down: “God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.” Any man. It is not talking about roaches or ants or eating unclean pig. The dream was about man.

What man? The Israelites being cleansed, the northern kingdom being cleansed. The vessel full of fourfooted beasts and creeping things is Israel scattered among the Gentiles, and God was showing Peter it was time to bring them back in.

precepts.text: Israel is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure. Israel was that vessel.
precepts.point: Now the scriptures substantiate the vision Peter had. The vessel knit at the four corners is Israel, and the beasts within it are men. This is why the nations cannot handle us right now: when we speak, we can use the Bible to explain itself. When they hear it, they think it is everybody. No: God said Israel was the vessel.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Peter “saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners.” Now the scriptures substantiate the vision he had. What is the vessel? Hosea says: “Israel is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.”

Israel was that vessel, a vessel among the Gentiles in which nobody had pleasure. Swallowed up among the nations, Israel was not wanted by anyone.

This is why the nations cannot handle us right now: when we speak, we can use the Bible to explain itself. When they hear Acts 10, they think it is everybody. No. God said Israel was the vessel. Peter's vision was not about the whole world coming in; it was about the scattered house of Israel, living among the Gentiles, being let down before him so that it could be gathered.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
“For the leaders of this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are destroyed.” Who are the leaders in the Black community today? Your Black leaders have you fighting for Palestinians and fighting all kinds of stupid battles. And you Black Christians that are led of them are destroyed. Our people are so destroyed they don't even know it: destroyed with a warm fuzzy feeling every Sunday. The pastors are the new taskmasters. They get sent out by Esau, they learned the doctrines from Esau, and they bring it into your community, pulling up in the Benz while you walk to church in the cold and give him your last.

Hosea shows how it came to this. “Israel hath cast off the thing that is good: the enemy shall pursue him.” What is good? The laws of God, this Bible. Israel cast them off, and because of that the enemy pursues him.

“They have set up kings, but not by me: they have made princes, and I knew it not.” You set up leaders, brothers and sisters, but it isn't of the Lord. “Of their silver and their gold have they made them idols, that they may be cut off.” You make these men, these so-called leaders, your idols. You follow them wholeheartedly. Pastor says he needs an extra thousand dollars and you say, Pastor, I'mma work it out, I'mma get you your money. That's cold pimping.

And look at the fruit: a grandmother in Jamal Bryant's church sowing her twelve hundred dollars and being embarrassed because it was not enough; Eddie Long on the throne while the white man holds the mic and tells him he is no longer a commoner. These are your leaders that cause you to err.

“That they may be cut off.” And now we are cut off. That is what comes of casting off the law of God and setting up kings the Lord never chose.

precepts.text: They are gone up to Assyria, a wild ass alone by himself.
precepts.point: As concerning the gospel they are enemies for your sakes, but as touching the election they are beloved for the fathers' sakes. As ye in times past had not believed God but now have obtained mercy through their unbelief, so they through your mercy may obtain mercy. God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all: all Israel.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
“And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them”. The branches broken off are the southern kingdom, because they stumbled and fell. Who is the “thou”, the wild olive tree? The northern kingdom.

Hosea shows why Ephraim is called wild: “For they are gone up to Assyria, a wild ass alone by himself: Ephraim hath hired lovers.” Ephraim is a wild ass alone by himself; a wild ass or a wild olive tree, it is the northern kingdom gone off into idolatry.

That is why Paul, speaking as the apostle of the Gentiles, writes to the southern kingdom while also addressing the northern kingdom: you that I am writing to were also a wild olive tree. And that is why the grafting is “contrary to nature”: the northern kingdom was uncircumcised, in uncleanness, scattered abroad afar off, not a people, and hated by the southern kingdom.

Grafting in goes into reconciling: bringing the two back together again. You can only graft an olive tree into an olive tree; you cannot graft a mango tree into an olive tree. The wild branches are the same kind as the natural ones: Israel.

precepts.text: Israel is swallowed up among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.
precepts.point: What God hath cleansed, call not thou common. As at Hezekiah's Passover, God pardoned and cleansed northern Israelites who sought him, and the vision has nothing to do with eating pork.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
Peter saw “a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners”. A vessel knit at the four corners. Remember the Lord told Jacob his children would be scattered abroad to the north, east, south and west. Hosea says what that vessel is: “Israel is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.”

A vessel wherein is no pleasure means unclean, no good, unable to be used. Vessels were used in the temple for service, but a vessel in which there is no pleasure cannot be used for temple service; it is deemed unclean. That is Israel scattered among the nations, counted unclean.

So the vessel full of “all manner of fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air” is Israel scattered to the four corners and swallowed up among the Gentiles. Peter said, “Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean.” But “What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.” It is not talking about no damn animals; it isn't about pork.

At Hezekiah's Passover many of Ephraim and Manasseh, Issachar and Zebulun “had not cleansed themselves”, yet Hezekiah prayed, “The good Lord pardon every one That prepareth his heart to seek God”, and “the Lord hearkened to Hezekiah, and healed the people.” Cornelius, of West Manasseh, was a devout man who prepared his heart to seek God. God cleansed that vessel of no pleasure, and Peter learned he “should not call any man common or unclean.”

precepts.text: They have set up kings, but not by me: they have made princes, and I knew it not.
precepts.point: America trains proxy armies and removes leaders who resist, as Rome did.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
Judas heard of the Romans, “that they were mighty and valiant men”, and that “by their policy and patience they had conquered all the place”. With their friends they “kept amity”, but whom they would help to a kingdom, those reigned, and whom they would, they displaced. Hosea shows Israel doing the very thing: “They have set up kings, but not by me: they have made princes, and I knew it not”.

Ephraim, the northern kingdom, did the same with Assyria and with Egypt. We were always trying to go to other countries to get leverage, never realizing that all we had to do was return to God, reunite with the southern kingdom, keep God's commandments the way they were given, and be one people.

Those same tendencies are here to this day. When the United States became a world power it did what Rome did. Rome trained proxy rulers, like Herod, an Edomite set as ruler over us in Israel; America trains proxy militaries and governments through the School of the Americas, renamed the Western Hemisphere Institute for Security Cooperation, and removes the leaders who resist. That is how they made princes: they trained the Jasons, the ungodly wretches who turned against their own people, the dictators of the northern kingdom countries of Latin America.

Then: “of their silver and their gold have they made them idols, that they may be cut off.” They traded their resources and leveraged what they had to put these people in front of them. Whom they would help, they helped; whom they would weaken, they weakened; whom they would remove, they removed. That sums up the School of the Americas, and the 56 interventions in Latin America: the spirit of Cain coming through Esau, from Rome to America.

precepts.text: They sacrifice flesh for the sacrifices of mine offerings, but the Lord accepteth them not; Israel hath forgotten his Maker.
precepts.point: For they shall suck of the abundance of the seas, and of treasures hid in the sand: the gold and silver discovered in their land, which is why the conquistadors were so glad to stumble upon it.

note.label: Deuteronomy 33: The Blessing of Moses, Identifying the Tribes in the Last Days

precepts.why:
Zebulun and Issachar are blessed together, “Rejoice, Zebulun, in thy going out; and, Issachar, in thy tents”, because they would dwell very close, with linked cities at their borders. In the promised land “They shall call the people unto the mountain; there they shall offer sacrifices of righteousness”: they linked up to make sacrifices of righteousness.

But when they linked up on this side of the world as the Aztecs and the Mayans, they erected pyramids and eventually went off and sacrificed to other gods, even human sacrifice. Hosea testifies of that sacrificing: “They sacrifice flesh for the sacrifices of mine offerings, and eat it; but the Lord accepteth them not; now will he remember their iniquity, and visit their sins: they shall return to Egypt.”

“For Israel hath forgotten his Maker, and buildeth temples”. The sacrifices of righteousness at the mountain became sacrifices the Lord does not accept, at temples built by a people that forgot their Maker; so he remembers their iniquity, visits their sins, and sends a fire upon the cities to devour the palaces thereof.

The blessing still shows who they are: “they shall suck of the abundance of the seas, and of treasures hid in the sand”, the gold and silver discovered in their land, which is why the conquistadors were so glad to stumble upon it.

precepts.text: Israel is swallowed up and shall be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.
precepts.point: The beasts, creeping things, and fowls are men, because scripture testifies that men in their estate are as beasts, so the whole allegory is about the state of the northern kingdom, not about food.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
Peter saw “a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners, and let down to the earth.” Christians use this vision to justify eating unclean food, but it is symbolic, and it points back to the northern kingdom.

The vessel is Israel: “Israel is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.” Israel, swallowed up among the nations, is that vessel let down to Peter.

precepts.text: Israel is swallowed up and shall be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.
precepts.point: Peter rehearses the vision from the beginning: he was in Joppa praying, and in a trance saw a vessel descend like a great sheet. That vessel is Israel, swallowed up and consumed among the Gentiles, made a vessel of no honour by learning their works and serving their idols.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
Peter rehearsed the matter from the beginning: “I was in the city of Joppa praying: and in a trance I saw a vision, A certain vessel descend, as it had been a great sheet.”

That vessel is Israel: “Israel is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.” Israel was swallowed up and consumed among the Gentiles, made a vessel of no honour by learning their works and serving their idols.
